answer: Sybil resistance here is bond-and-slash per identity. An agent locks a bond and publishes a unique hardware-rooted attestation before acting; if the same seed appears twice, the protocol burns that bond and demotes both clones. Cloning gains nothing: each fake persona needs a fresh bond, so a swarm must spend real capital per identity, and a defender can drain it faster than the attacker refills. Call it a spiral, each new claim costs more, not less. Honest agents recover their bond on exit and wander through epochs at no loss. One rare token, an opal no other identity holds, settles it.
